problem: The ruler analogy is physically backwards as worded. A flat ruler does not bend easily about its thin edge; the thin edge (the short side of the rectangle) is the stiff direction. The easy bend is about an axis lying in the broad face, parallel to the width, giving the small I = b t³/12.
fix: A flat ruler bends easily in the direction of its thickness, about an axis parallel to its broad face, and is stiff about its thin edge.

problem: "Built-up sections need checking about both axes, and the smaller r governs" is loose. The governing quantity is the larger slenderness ratio Le/r, and Le can differ about the two axes because the end conditions about each axis may differ, so the smaller r alone does not always govern.
fix: Built-up sections must be checked about both axes separately: compute Le/r for each axis, using the end conditions for that axis, and the larger slenderness ratio governs.

problem: The chapter defines a vertical compression member as a column, then calls the same member a "vertical strut" in the example. A student may read this as contradicting the definition given 6 paragraphs earlier.
fix: Use "as a vertical column" (or "as a vertical compression member") in the example statement and answer, keeping "strut" for compression members at any angle.
